notes: DS-ECO-6: the corpus fallback's own second sentence ('nothing organised behind it') is the exact line the brief lists as a refusal on a town whose rows carry Street gang and Front businesses. The claim I was told to keep and the card conflict, so I kept the 'minor' tier and dropped the denial.

DS-ECO-12 income mix: the corpus fallback uses 'you will be given', which breaks the no-`will` bar and the address-to-the-reader tell, so the claim had to be re-shaped rather than followed; and the pool key says two or three sources while the field says ten rows, with no way to state either without a count.

DS-GEN-18 STALLED: the stated move order is INSTITUTION then PRESENT, but the corpus spine given as the claim opens on {settlement}; it also carries a semicolon and 'the books', both barred. Also unclear whether an institution fill may be lower-cased mid-sentence, so the fill string was kept verbatim after 'The'.

The rule that a second sentence must rest on a listed field and name it in its own word is unsatisfiable where every listed field is DERIVED or UNREADABLE (C3, POSTURE), so those units are one sentence; it is not said whether one sentence is the intended outcome or a thinning.

Stances are given per pool (visitor, street, threshold, counterforce) but with zero faces and a spine that must stand bare in the archiver's hand, the stance has no carrier; 'threshold' and 'counterforce' are also outside the brief's three named stances.

The MARKET-OPEN corpus line is itself an ORIGIN ('the market was where the carts already stopped ... grew around the habit'), which the brief names verbatim as the one refusal with no exception. 'Keep the claim, do not imitate the breach' leaves it unstated whether the claim survives at all once the founding frame is removed; I kept the present-state half.

Four more corpus lines carry constructions the brief vetoes: a colon (scores.monster), a which-clause closer (economicViability, foodSecurity), not-X-but-Y (road) and the barred word 'will' (prominentRelationship). Since the corpus line is both the claim and the fallback, it is unclear whether a line that keeps the claim but drops the device still counts as keeping it.

DS-GEN-5 'ordinary' and DS-GEN-6 'road' set opposite relations to the same road on the same page (the town takes little from the traffic; the road is a condition of the town). The refusal test is defined against card fields and page lines only, so nothing says which yields or whether they must be written to coexist.

Every pool lists 'faces to write: 0' and 'notebook: none', so the entire seating apparatus (one face per seated source, pairs, compromised roll, the ten roles rosters) and the whole DM notebook register are unused, even though the page declares audience dm. The instruction 'on audience dm, notebook carries one row per dm-only face the card lists' and 'that number is zero' only agree by accident here.

Three pools (prosperity, readiness label, foodSecurity) list `name = "Spitzplatz"` as their only field, while a second sentence must 'rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word'. That makes a second sentence possible only by naming the town, which ruling 12 and the slot-fill rule both restrain, so those units are effectively capped at one sentence with no rule saying so. Separately, DS-REL-2 names two bodies (Berchta Schmidt, Karl Berger) that the town block licenses to act and speak but the pack's 'never a minted proper NAME' forbids in a pooled line; I wrote around the names.

Two pools (DS-ECO-12 INCOME MIX and DS-GEN-18 STALLED) give their corpus-fallback spine with a hard-bar violation baked in (INCOME MIX's fallback uses 'will'; STALLED's fallback uses a semicolon) -- the brief says not to imitate the breach, so I rewrote both to keep the claim without the banned construction, but a model working faster could easily reproduce the breach since the fallback is presented as authoritative.

The dm-only pool (DS-ECO-6) has a genuine tension: the pool's own instruction says notebook is empty and the note-register content 'rides in spine', but PART V of the brief caps notebook devices/registers at two sentences and describes the notebook as a distinct field from spine -- it is not fully clear whether the refuter's mechanical scan (e.g. the ellipsis/colon allowance) even applies to a spine field on a dm-only pool, since every other rule ties those devices to 'dm-only faces' or 'notebook', never to 'spine'.

For fields marked DERIVED (prosperityRank, exportPosture.status) the brief says a second sentence must 'rest on' the field 'and name it in its own word' while also saying a DERIVED field 'cannot carry a value of its own' -- these two constraints are in tension (rest on it vs. give it nothing) and I resolved it by naming the field's topic without a value judgment, but the brief never states how a refuter actually adjudicates that boundary.

STALLED's move order V5 (INSTITUTION then PRESENT) and its second-sentence-must-name-a-field rule interact awkwardly with the corpus fallback's own single semicolon-joined sentence structure -- restructuring it into one long comma/and-joined sentence to dodge the semicolon bar and the second-sentence field requirement simultaneously left me unsure whether that reading of 'sentence' (one clause chain vs. true single sentence) matches the instruments' own parser.

The brief states colons are 'licensed on dm-only faces only' but the corpus fallback for a non-dm-only pool (COMBINATION C3) uses a colon anyway as 'the claim and the fallback' -- it is unclear whether colon is a hard refuter bar on ordinary spines or only a selector taste preference, since it is absent from THE MECHANICAL BARS list.

Two seats name sources this town does not seat: 'garrison' (Internal Security face 5, Economic Survival face 1) and 'elders' (Invasion & War face 0) appear in neither the town block's roles nor its sources, and forceBuckets.garrison is false. I took the brief's 'nothing to stand on' rule and copied the corpus row verbatim at those three seats, but the turn still seats them as if the roles resolved.

That verbatim rule collides with the mechanical bars on the elders seat: its corpus face is unrendered ('{elders} {v:take} the walls...'), while the bars forbid raw identifiers on the page and the brief says to write the rendered words. Copying verbatim and rendering cannot both be satisfied; I copied verbatim, so that face carries tokens.
The Invasion & War pool says 'slots you may use: (none)' and then declares a fill for {court}. No pool declares {court} as usable, so the fill is unreachable; I used no slot there.

'The second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is ambiguous for pools with faces: the drawn unit is spine plus one face, so it is unclear whether a face counts as that second sentence. It is also unclear what 'its own word' is for a purely numeric reading (defenseProfile.readiness.score = 57, defenseProfile.scores.economic = 76) when digits are barred. I wrote single-sentence spines throughout to avoid the question.

The page is audience dm, but every pool says 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.', so the notebook register the brief specifies at length has nowhere to appear on a dm page. Separately, 'structure organized' says to write one sentence and no second while its own corpus fallback is two sentences; I wrote one.

Audience is dm, yet every one of the ten pools says 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.' and 'faces to write: 0'. So the whole dm page is nine bare spines with no notebook and no faces — the brief's entire DM register, pair machinery, compromised roll and observed/public candidates are unreachable on this turn. If that is intended the turn should say so; if not, the card is not giving the dm tab its rows.

In DS-POW-4 'riskLabel: Holding' the slots {seat} and {faction} are BOTH filled with 'Guild Council', and the corpus line compares them ('holds because {faction} is still the heavier of the two'). Filled literally that reads as the body being heavier than itself. I dropped the comparison and kept the rest of the claim; the fills need disambiguating.

Three pools (DS-POW-1 x2, DS-POW-4 'riskLabel') all carry order V5 'INSTITUTION then PRESENT' with the same single institution slot, so three units on one page necessarily open on the Guild Council. The brief's own tell list says two pools opening the same way means autopilot, and nothing in the turn offers a second institution row to lead with.

The 'legitimacyHold' pool records only govMultiplier = 1.15 and permits a second sentence only if it 'rests on one of these fields and names it in its own word' — but the mechanical bars forbid digits and raw identifiers, so that field can never be named. I wrote one sentence. Same tension in the DORMANT pool, whose only field is marked DERIVED and therefore also unusable.

Two instructions on naming the town pull against each other across a page of nine units: each pool declares {settlement} and says 'WRITE THE FILL, NOT THE TOKEN', while the brief says name the town at most once in a unit and never as the first word of two units, and ruling 12 prefers 'the town' or 'here'. I used Spitzplatz once on the page and wrote around it elsewhere; the turn does not say whether a declared slot must actually be spent.

Several of this page's fallback CORPUS LINEs break the brief's own bars, so they cannot be reused verbatim as the model's answer even though the brief calls them 'the line that ships if yours is refused': MARKET-OPEN's corpus line reads as a founding-stated-as-record ('the market was where the carts already stopped'), which is the exact pattern the brief separately calls out as refused; road's corpus line uses the barred 'not X but Y' construction; ADMINISTERED, scores.monster, scores.internal, scores.magical and tier-overlay all open on the bare {settlement} token, which together would violate 'never as the first word of two units on one page' if taken as given; scores.magical's and the ordinary-route corpus lines use a semicolon (mechanically barred); and prominentRelationship's corpus line uses 'will'/'will not', the barred future indicative. The brief gives no guidance on how to reconcile 'the corpus is the claim you must keep' with 'do not imitate the breach' when nearly every corpus line on one page is itself in breach.

Several pools' 'THE FIELDS this pool reads' entries are given only as opaque summaries rather than usable values (e.g. MARKET-OPEN's readings is marked wholly UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD apart from two named sub-fields; ADMINISTERED's readings.inst is printed as a bare list of flag NAMES like hasMagesGuild/hasWizardTower with no true/false shown), so the instruction that 'the second sentence... must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is only loosely satisfiable for those pools — there is no way to know which institution flags are actually true.

The page header says 'audience dm', but every one of the 17 pools on this page independently specifies 'faces to write: 0' and 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.' so nothing on this rendered page actually differs between a dm render and a player render; unclear whether that is intended (this tab simply has no dm-only content) or a card-construction gap.

Ruling 12 is stated twice with different scopes right next to each other in the brief ('{settlement} appears in at most one unit of a pool' vs. the slot-fill instruction's 'never as the first word of two units on one page') and it is not fully clear whether the page-wide version is meant to bind across unrelated pools/blocks that a game master would never see rendered side by side, or only within one pool's own variant set.

The ordinary-route pool (DS-GEN-5, 'ordinary (route road and the default)') lists the {settlement} slot twice in its slot table with an identical fill both times, which reads like a duplicate/copy-paste line rather than two distinct slots.

turn.md gives four distinct 'stance' values (unfolding, visitor, street, counterforce) but brief.md only ever names three stances (ledger, street, visitor) as surviving 'AS THE SPINE LINE'S TAG'; 'unfolding' and 'counterforce' are undefined, so it is unclear whether they should shape the spine beyond the explicit per-pool ORDER and field instructions. Resolved by treating spine as always-bare per the explicit STANCE rule and ignoring the tag's effect on wording.

The shipped corpus fallback line for DS-POW-2 'recentConflict present' contains a semicolon, which the mechanical bars explicitly forbid everywhere - a live example of the brief's own warning that the corpus line 'is not a model of the law' and may itself breach a hard bar.

For DS-POW-2 'recentConflict present' the given recentConflict field states an elapsed duration ('three months'); it is unclear whether a number WORD sourced directly from a given field (as opposed to an invented one) is licensed prose, since floor 2 bars 'no count' with no carve-out stated for field-sourced durations. Resolved conservatively by omitting the specific duration and using a non-numeric elapsed-course phrase instead.

Two pools (DS-POW-4 'riskLabel: Holding' and 'legitimacyHold: public backing hardens the hold') fill both the {seat} and {faction} slots with the identical value 'Guild Council', collapsing what the corpus template implies are two distinct parties (a seat-holder and a rival/backing faction) into one; the brief gives no guidance for phrasing the relational claim naturally when the two slots coincide.

Every non-omitted pool on this dm-tab page carries zero notebook rows and no audience-specific field data, so nothing in this render actually exercises dm-only content (notebook is empty for all nine units); the page distinguishes 'dm' from 'player' only in principle here, not in any material this turn supplied.

DS-DEF-2 assigns speaking faces to 'elders' (Invasion & War) and 'garrison' (Internal Security, Economic Survival), but town.md's own roles/sources lists have no elders or garrison roster for this town-tier settlement (forceBuckets.garrison is false), so no lawful attribution phrase exists for them; resolved by copying the given corpus face verbatim at those seats per the brief's own 'nothing to stand on' rule, but the card contradicts itself here.

Several pool corpus spines (e.g. Economic Survival, Disasters & Famine, DS-DEF-5 charter hall) are attributed accounts, not bare archiver facts, even though the brief's general STANCE section says a spine is 'always... bare, on the document's own authority'; resolved by reading each pool's stance tag (ledger/street/visitor/etc.) as governing spine voice, since the shipped corpus itself does this.

DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War' pool says 'slots you may use: (none)' but then supplies a {court} fill value anyway; treated as informational (the seeded court-role draw for that face) rather than a usable token, since no token was actually declared.

The instruction that 'the second sentence of a unit... must rest on one of these fields' does not say whether it binds the spine's second sentence, a face's second sentence, or the combined rendered draw; every second sentence written was kept thematically tied to the pool's given field to satisfy it either way.

Ruling 42c (grain store not granary, sick house not infirmary) sits alongside an earlier 'class 2 dated NAME-words are unrestricted' claim that would keep 'granary'; followed the later, more specific 42c throughout since the brief states the archaism licence was withdrawn.

The STALLED pool's slot fill says {institution} is "Cartographer's guild", but the town block's institutions list holds "Cartographer's workshop" and no guild of that name. The brief bars naming a body the card does not carry, so the fill and the roster contradict each other. I followed the fill, as the turn instructs, but this is the one line on the page I could not make lawful on both readings.

Two pools (COMBINATION C3, POSTURE: established) list only a DERIVED field, and the rule that a second sentence must rest on a read field collides with the rule that a DERIVED reading carries no value of its own. It is unclear whether those pools may have a second sentence at all. I wrote two sentences for the first (the underlying economicState.prosperity = "Comfortable" is printed, so there is a value to rest on) and one for the second (no input is given at all).

The audience is dm, yet every pool says the notebook holds no rows. The DM register, the shades and the feelings occupy a large part of the brief and are unreachable on this page, so the dm and player outputs are identical here. If that is intended it would be cheaper to say so once at the top of the turn.

The mechanical bar forbids the word "week", but the town's own institution roster prints "Weekly market" as a nameable row. A writer who names that row breaks the bar and a writer who avoids it loses a licensed particular. I used the plain "market" instead.

The phrase "name it in its own word" for the second sentence's field is not defined. It could mean the field's engine name (barred as a schema word), its printed value, or a plain-English paraphrase of what it measures. I read it as the third.

Seat/roster mismatch: the turn seats faces on `watch`, `court`, `guild`, `hall`, `gate`, `muster` and `garrison`, but the town block's `roles` and `sources` list only elders, market, public, register, stranger and tavern, and the bars refuse any role the town does not seat. Nothing in the turn says which rule wins; I applied the brief's 'copy the corpus verbatim when the card gives a face nothing to stand on', so 11 of the 30 faces are verbatim corpus rows.

Audience is `dm`, yet every one of the 14 pools says 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.' The entire notebook register (PART V, rulings 17/29-33, four shades and seven feelings) is therefore unexercised on a DM page. Unclear whether that is the card's intent or a missing input.

The rule 'the second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is ambiguous once a unit is spine plus a drawn face: it does not say whether the count runs over the spine alone or over the rendered spine+face pair. It is also unsatisfiable as written for pools whose only field is `institutions = "[29 rows]"` or a DERIVED/UNREADABLE reading, since there is no value to name. I kept every spine on a pool with faces to one sentence to avoid the question.

The pool 'First-Survey qualification (the reading is a first look)' has as its whole claim the document qualifying its own reading, which is exactly what ruling 40 and the E2 ratchet refuse on the fair copy ('the survey finds', 'so far as the survey can find'). The pool key and the law point opposite ways; I wrote the claim as what is and is not out in the open rather than omit the pool.

Card-internal contradictions I had to write around: `armedForces.standing`, `contracted` and `fortifications` are empty and forceBuckets garrison/militia/watch are all false, while the page's guardEffectivenessDesc asserts a mercenary company provides enforcement (I wrote 'no soldiers of its own'); `compromised` is empty while `compromisedRate` is 0.7; the town seats an 'Alehouse' but the source is named `tavern`; and the DS-DEF-2 Invasion corpus spine contains 'its week', a word the mechanical bars forbid outright, so it could not be imitated.

Town card's `roles` array seats only six sources (elders, market, public, register, stranger, tavern), but several pools direct faces through sources absent from that array (hall, guild, watch, court, muster, gate, garrison) as though they were seated. Treated as the card giving that face nothing to stand on and copied the corpus face verbatim at those seats, per the brief's own fallback rule.

Ruling 42c withdraws 'pedlar' and 'alehouse' as archaic and mandates modern replacements, but the town's own stranger/tavern rosters (and turn.md's explicit override list for one face) print exactly those words as the only permitted attribution phrasing. Worked around it by choosing other roster options (drover, rider who stopped a night, potboy, woman at the long table) where the roster offered them; flagging the underlying contradiction since it will not always have a safe alternative.

Pool 'Invasion & War: neither walls nor force' is tagged stance 'street' but its given corpus spine is written in the 'public' collective-perception form ('everyone has seen... and takes it that'), not a town-talk register. Followed the corpus's own shape rather than the stance label, since the stance tags are described as guidance and the corpus line is the standing claim.

The corpus line for pool 'UNWALLED-SMALL' contains a semicolon, which the mechanical bars forbid outright. Per the brief's explicit instruction not to imitate a breach in the corpus line, rewrote it as two sentences instead of copying the punctuation.

Pool 'readiness WEAK' (DS-DEF-1) and the page's own [badge]/[row] readiness figures use overlapping vocabulary (readiness, posture) across two declared-separate ladders; wrote to the pool key's sense of the field without naming the posture badge word 'Lightly Defended,' but the brief does not fully spell out how far a spine may lean on the word 'readiness' itself without brushing the badge ladder.

The STALLED pool's turn.md fill gives {institution} as "Cartographer's guild", but the town card's own institutions list spells the same row "Cartographer's workshop" — the fill and the roster disagree on the institution's name; I followed the explicit "write the fill, not the token" instruction and used the turn's spelling.

brief.md never gives a normative definition of how the three stance tags (ledger/street/visitor) should be realized on a spine that has zero faces; I inferred ledger = a bare archiver statement (ruling 40), street = the public/town-talk voice, visitor = an attributed stranger account, by triangulating from the Part IV stance description and the ruling-40/28 material, but this mapping for the SPINE specifically (as opposed to faces) is not stated outright.

For INCOME MIX and STALLED, the listed FIELDS are opaque placeholders (e.g. economicState.incomeSources = "[4 rows]", resourceAnalysis.exploitation = "{}") rather than actual values, so the specific magnitude in each pool's corpus line (a strong majority from one trade; a supply failure upstream) cannot be independently checked against the given fields — I preserved those claims only because the brief states the corpus line is the claim to keep, not because the FIELDS section itself supports the magnitude.

Several mechanisms the brief leans on for spine/face variety (the archiver-observed face, the public-tagged candidate, the compromised-role candidate) are marked in brief.md as tied to cars not yet landed in the build, but the output schema has no tagging field at all, so it is unclear whether a model in this harness is meant to use those forms freely in plain prose or avoid them as not-yet-authorized.

The SECURE pool (DS-ECO-9) supplies no readable fields and no slots at all, so its one permitted sentence has nothing pool-specific to rest on beyond the page's own printed foodSecurity badge line — worth flagging since every other pool at least offers a field or a slot to write from.

Stance 'counterforce' (pool 'Tolerated') is not one of the three stances the brief documents for a spine tag (ledger / street / visitor); nothing says what it asks of the line, so it was written as a plain bare fact.

The card seats no hall, guild, watch, muster or gate source and lists no town-hall institution row, yet several corpus fallback spines say 'the hall'. Unclear whether 'the hall' counts as a body this village carries; it was avoided and the seat named by its slot fill instead.

Ruling 42c bars 'the reeve' as an archaism while the card's own institution row is 'Village reeve' and the {seat} fill is 'Elected Reeve'. The fill was written verbatim as instructed, but the two instructions point opposite ways.

'legitimacyHold' is the only pool with a recorded field, and its value is a bare multiplier of one. The digit bar and the no-number-as-record floor leave no way to state that value, so the second sentence it licenses was not taken.

Two DS-POW-1/DS-POW-4 pools read adjacent legitimacy fields that sit oddly together on one page (standing favourable and drawn from prosperity, versus public opinion neither helping nor hurting). The two-ladders and two-fields guidance covers the badge/band and funding cases by name but not this pair.

Every pool says 'faces to write: 0' and 'notebook: none', yet the page header says 'audience dm'. So the dm audience produced nothing dm-specific: no notebook row anywhere, and the whole brief's notebook register (PART V, the shades, the feelings, the clarity test) is unusable on this page. If that is intended it is a lot of prompt for zero output; if it is not, the card is not passing the dm rows through.

The second-sentence rule ('must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word') is unsatisfiable for three pools whose only listed field is name = "Hochhausen" (prosperity, readiness label, foodSecurity) and for the two axis pools whose readable field is readings.scores, a bag of digits the mechanical bars forbid printing. I wrote one sentence in those, which loses the pair/contrast moves the brief most wants.

GARRISONED (DS-GEN-17) reads against the town block: forceBuckets garrison/militia/watch are all false, armedForces.standing/contracted/fortifications are empty, and no watch or muster is in the sources list, yet the corpus claim I must keep is 'the town keeps professionals for its safety'. The only armed row the card carries is the Adventurers' charter hall, so I leaned the whole unit on that; a reader could still call the claim and the buckets a contradiction.

The pack's 'never a minted proper NAME' (PART I §3) and the mechanical bar 'every body you name must be a row this card carries' point opposite ways for the prominentRelationship pool, whose whole subject is Ingrid Köhler and Ivo Werner. I named them once, on the ground that the machine line on the same page already prints both names.

Three corpus lines I had to keep break bars the same prompt calls fatal: two carry semicolons (GARRISONED, scores.monster), one carries a colon (economicViability), and prominentRelationship's line is built on 'will and will not do', which ruling 33 bars outright. The brief does say not to imitate a breach, but a fallback line that would itself be dropped by the instruments is an odd safety net. Separately, the page-level rules about the settlement slot ('at most one unit of a pool', 'never the first word of two units on one page') do not say whether 18 units across 8 blocks count as one page, so I used the name twice and opened with it once.
Pool DS-GEN-3 foodSecurity.label used stance "threshold", which is not one of the three canonical stances the brief defines (ledger/street/visitor); its intended register had to be inferred.

Pool DS-GEN-17 GARRISONED gives readings.inst only as a list of field names (a schema shape), not actual boolean values, so no specific institution (e.g. hasGarrison, hasWatch) could be asserted; kept to the corpus's general claim only.

The DS-REL-2 prominentRelationship corpus line itself contains 'will and will not do', which breaches the brief's own no-will/shall mechanical bar; per the brief's instruction not to imitate a breach, the written spine avoids 'will' entirely.
The DS-GEN-3 foodSecurity corpus line uses a which-clause closer, a construction PART III of the brief lists as tired prose (a taste tell, not a hard bar); avoided in the written version regardless.

Several DS-GEN-3 pools (prosperity, readiness.label, scores.internal, scores.economic's name field, tier overlay's name field) list only `name = Hochhausen` under 'fields', which is not a substantive second fact — treated as equivalent to no field, so each spine stayed to one sentence rather than risk an unsupported second sentence being withheld.

Two of the 9 pools the turn lists (DS-POW-2 'governing faction holds a NARROW plurality', DS-POW-7 'layer DORMANT') were explicitly marked NOT WRITEABLE ON THIS TOWN with instructions to omit; the output correctly contains 7 units, not 9.

Several corpus fallback spines (pools 1, 3, 4/mixed, 6/riskLabel) are themselves two sentences, but the per-pool instruction for every field-less pool says 'write ONE sentence and no second' -- I compressed each into a single sentence rather than imitating the corpus's two-sentence shape; this reading seems right but the brief never states outright that the sentence cap overrides the corpus's own sentence count.

The corpus line for the PROSPERITY pool uses a colon, but the notebook-devices section (PART V) implies the colon is licensed only on dm-only/notebook faces, not the player fair copy -- I avoided colons throughout on that reading, though the brief never says explicitly that a colon breaks a bar on the spine.

For the legitimacyHold pool the card supplies a concrete field value (govMultiplier = 1) and says a second sentence 'if there is one' must rest on it named in words; I kept it to one sentence expressing neutrality in prose rather than risk mis-naming a numeric field in words, since the brief gives no worked example of naming a multiplier-type field in plain words.

The rule 'never {settlement} as the first word of two units on one page' forced a rewrite of one spine (legitimacyHold) that originally opened on 'Hochhausen' like the riskLabel spine; the brief doesn't say whether this same-opener constraint is a hard bar or a PART III taste tell, so I treated it as the stricter reading (hard constraint) to be safe.
